Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-30
Time: 16:00 PT / 23:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Sarah Nguyen (CISO, Veritas), Tom Brooks (Head of Platform, Veritas), Elena Park (Security Engineer, Veritas)

Auto-generated Summary (brief):
- Discovery focused on security posture for evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment.
- Key topics: SOC 2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML + SCIM, RBAC, audit logs & retention, encryption/KMS/BYOK, data residency and deletion policies.
- Next steps: share SOC2 artifacts, architecture diagram for private/VPC, schedule demo of SAML/SCIM & RBAC, pilot dedicated capacity benchmarks.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, i think we have about 45 minutes, uh i'll run quick intros and then hand over to Liam for the deep security bits — um Sarah, Tom, Elena thanks for taking the time.
[00:12] Sarah: thanks Maya, appreciate it. quick overview — i'm Sarah, CISO at Veritas Systems. we are evaluating options for embedding LLM-based features into our platform, but security and compliance are table-stakes so this call is mainly about how Redwood protects customer data and supports our compliance needs.
[00:30] Tom: yep, i'm Tom, head of platform, i'll be tuning into network/VPC requirements and deployment models.
[00:36] Elena: Elena here, security engineer; i'll be looking at logs, encryption, key mgmt, and auditability.
[00:42] Liam: great — i'm Liam, solutions engineer, i'll cover architecture, KMS, RBAC, logs, SSO and answer any technical concerns. diego's here too for notes.

[01:05] Maya: ok first big question — SOC 2 and ISO. do you have a SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 cert or roadmap? what's in scope for hosted?
[01:16] Sarah: yes specific question: if we start with hosted (your public API) what parts of the stack are in-scope for Redwood vs Veritas.
[01:25] Liam: good q. high level: Redwood's hosted API is within our control plane and managed infra; for SOC 2 we have Type II attestation covering our control plane and hosted service operations. we also have an ISO 27001 ISMS in progress — we completed the gap assessment last quarter, audit scheduled for Q4. the hosted service scope includes model serving, infrastructure, logging and operational controls. in practice, your data in the request/response lifecycle is processed by us; you can enable retention controls and opt-in logging.
[01:54] Sarah: can you share the report? redacted is fine but we need the attestation.
[01:59] Maya: absolutely, we'll send the SOC 2 Type II and a pen test summary after the call. (action)

[02:10] Tom: for customers requiring strict isolation we may need dedicated pools or private deployment. can you explain the differences quickly (hosted vs dedicated vs private)? network wise how isolated are dedicated nodes?
[02:22] Liam: sure — hosted is multi-tenant, fastest to go live; dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools in a tenant-isolated fashion — it's single-tenant from a compute perspective but still managed by Redwood; network egress can be restricted, and you get dedicated capacity SLA. private deployment (VPC/private control plane or on-prem) gives you customer-managed network and optional air-gapped or VPC peering models — keys and encryption can be customer-managed in private mode. in dedicated we support private networking options and can do customer VPC peering in many regions.
[02:58] Elena: for dedicated, are keys stored in Redwood KMS or can we bring our own key (BYOK)? also HSM support?
[03:06] Liam: BYOK is available for private and dedicated with certain contract tiers — we can integrate with your AWS KMS or Azure Key Vault. HSM-backed keys are supported for private deployments; for hosted we use our managed KMS, and we can provide an attestation of cryptographic controls but BYOK/HSM typically requires Private or Dedicated with contractual terms.
[03:32] Sarah: ok audit logs — what do you capture, retention options, and can logs be forwarded to our SIEM?
[03:40] Liam: we capture request metadata, request/response hashes (you can opt-out of storing full content), user/account IDs, model version, latency metrics, and operational events (deploys, scaling). audit logs can be forwarded to customer endpoints: CloudWatch, Splunk, or syslog/HTTPS for SIEM ingestion. retention is configurable per-account; default retention on hosted is 90 days for full content, 365 for metadata, but we can adjust per contractual requirements for Dedicated/Private.
[04:16] Elena: are logs immutable and tamper-evident? we need chain-of-custody for some workflows.
[04:23] Liam: logs are write-once in our system and we maintain integrity checks; for stronger guarantees we can support log forwarding to your own storage (S3 with MFA delete or to an append-only SIEM). for private deployments you can manage the storage to meet your chain-of-custody.
[04:42] Tom: SSO and provisioning — do you support SAML SSO + SCIM for user provisioning and role sync?
[04:49] Liam: yes — SAML SSO is supported on the console, SCIM for provisioning, and we support OIDC for API auth patterns. RBAC is role-based with built-in roles (admin, developer, auditor) and granular resource policies for models and routes. we can map SAML groups to RBAC roles.
[05:12] Elena: can we enforce MFA and conditional access via our IdP?
[05:16] Liam: we honor IdP enforced MFA; conditional access policies are evaluated at the IdP level. in addition, we have session policies and token lifetimes configurable.
[05:27] Sarah: data residency and deletion — if we need EU data residency and the right to be forgotten, how is that handled?
[05:36] Liam: we have region routing policies; you can pin requests to EU-only regions for Hosted Dedicated in supported regions. for deletion, we offer delete APIs and can purge request/response content; permanent deletions depend on retention windows and backups. for strict residency and deletion compliance, Private or Dedicated with VPC and customer-managed storage is recommended.
[06:00] Tom: backups — are model caches or KV caches persisted to disk and backed up? any risk of customer data leaking via KV cache?
[06:10] Liam: KV cache is per-session and can be configured to not persist beyond the session; we have policies to scrub or never cache sensitive fields. for Dedicated/Private we can disable persistence and manage caches in customer-controlled storage to eliminate leakage risk.
[06:28] Maya: question from product — what's your process for vulnerabilities and disclosure? do you run regular pen tests and third-party assessments?
[06:36] Liam: we run internal security scans, annual third-party penetration tests, and have a bug bounty with triage. we'll share a summary of the most recent pentest; full reports are available under NDA. we also have a dedicated security contact for incident response.
[06:59] Elena: encryption in transit and at rest — TLS and AES-256? can we bring our own certs for private endpoints?
[07:06] Liam: TLS 1.2+ for in-transit; at-rest we use AES-256 and envelope encryption with KMS. for private deployment you can bring certs for endpoints and use your PKI; for hosted we manage certificates but support mutual TLS for certain integrations.
[07:27] Sarah: regulatory — do you support HIPAA, GDPR controls and data processing addendum (DPA)?
[07:33] Liam: yes we have a DPA and can sign business associate agreements for HIPAA-covered workflows in Dedicated/Private deployments; GDPR controls include data subject request support and data processing addendum. note: hosted has some constraints around ePHI by default — we recommend Private for strict HIPAA cases.
[07:56] Tom: what's the expected effort to stand up a private deployment in our VPC? network person-hours, firewall rules, and timeline?
[08:05] Liam: typical Private VPC deployment takes 4-6 weeks for standard configs: network setup, peering or VPN, KMS integration, and initial validation. effort typically 3-5 engineer-days on your side for firewall and route config, plus a Redwood infra engineer to orchestrate. we provide Terraform modules and a runbook.
[08:27] Elena: can you talk about endpoint authentication for APIs — are tokens short-lived, do you support mutual TLS or signed requests?
[08:34] Liam: API keys are short-lived tokens and we strongly recommend rotating keys; we also support OAuth2 client credential flows with tokens and mutual TLS for private endpoints. we have audit for token usage and automatic token revocation.
[08:51] Sarah: incident response — SLAs and notification timelines? we need 24/7 contact for high severity.
[08:58] Maya: we have escalation playbooks, 24/7 support for enterprise customers on Dedicated/Private and an on-call security team. severity 1 events have a 1-hour initial response and periodic updates.
[09:12] Tom: any customers doing BYOK + private who can be references?
[09:17] Liam: yes, we've worked with finserv and health customers — we can share anonymized case studies and put you in touch under NDA.
[09:25] Elena: one more technical — does Redwood retain model artifacts or fine-tune customer data? we want to ensure no inadvertent model training on customer prompts unless explicitly opted-in.
[09:36] Liam: we do not train shared models on customer prompt/response data by default. model training on customer data is opt-in and requires contractual terms. we can guarantee that hosted service doesn't use customer data for training without consent.
[09:53] Sarah: ok this has been helpful. can you also provide more detail on audit log schema — we need specific fields for our SIEM mapping.
[10:02] Liam: absolutely — i'll work with Elena to collect required fields; we'll include timestamps, request_id, user_id, account_id, model_id, route, src_ip, region, latency_ms, and hash of request/response if content is redacted.
[10:18] Elena: for the hash, we need a deterministic sha256 returned so we can validate integrity across systems.
[10:24] Liam: yes we can provide sha256 hex of payload, and timestamped signature for tamper evidence.
[10:31] Maya: ok i think good next steps, i'll recap — we'll send SOC2 report and pentest summary, Liam will send private deployment diagram and BYOK instructions, Elena will send log field list, and we'll schedule a follow-up demo focusing on SAML/SCIM and RBAC.
[10:46] Sarah: timeline wise, we are hoping to decide by end of September — pilot in October if it looks good.
[10:53] Tom: budget questions we can handle later, for now sec must be approved.
[10:57] Maya: perfect — thanks all. we'll follow up with the docs and set tentative cadence.
[11:05] Sarah: thanks Maya, Liam. bye.
[11:08] (call ends)
